summary.text: Your website sends enquiries to a contact email on a domain that is about to lapse, and your published head-office details disagree from page to page.
The award organiser's own hall of fame lists you as a 2025 winner, and Google reviewers give you a 4.7 rating, yet a contractor directory shows a lower grade than your site claims.
None of your newest Google reviews carries a reply from you, and your mobile homepage is slow on the phones most enquiries come from.

titles.f1: The domain behind your printed contact email expires soon, and your site's mail routing goes with it.
titles.f2: Anyone can send email that looks like it comes from your addresses, so a forged invoice can reach your client.
titles.f3: Your LinkedIn phone field holds part of your registration number, so a prospect who taps it cannot call you.
titles.f4: A contractor directory under your own registration number shows a dummy phone and hides your address.
titles.f5: Not one of your newest Google reviews has a reply from you, and the lone negative one sits unanswered.
titles.f6: Google reports your robots file as invalid, which weakens the search ranking your site claims for itself.
titles.f7: Your mobile homepage is slow to paint while your desktop version is instant, on the device most enquiries come from.
titles.c1: Your two websites give different head-office phone numbers, so one set of customers dials a line that may be stale.
titles.c2: Your head-office unit number appears three different ways, so couriers and survey teams can arrive at the wrong door.
titles.c3: Your branch list differs between your own two sites and a directory, so customers see different offices near them.
titles.c4: Your staff count reads three different ways on pages you control, so a bank or a candidate sees three companies.
titles.c5: A contractor directory shows a lower grade than your own site claims, which can rule you out of larger tenders.
titles.c6: Your completed-project count more than doubles depending on which page a prospect finds first.
titles.c7: A job board gives you a foreign legal form, so a customer or bank reads a company unsure of its own name.
titles.c8: Your two sites print different head-office emails, and one of them depends on the domain that is lapsing.
titles.n1: Worth checking: your only negative Google review carries the same name as one of your own engineers.
titles.n2: Worth checking why several of your five-star reviews landed on the same day.
titles.n3: A directory snippet attaches a different main phone number to your office; worth checking which line it belongs to.
titles.n4: Your revenue figure and an award profile's sales figure read as the same number; worth checking how a reader takes it.
titles.n5: Worth knowing that no tender awards, extortion listings or sanctions name you, which is a clean record rather than an achievement.
titles.n6: Google Maps sends visitors to one of your domains while your site calls another canonical; worth checking where that link lands.
